chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah al-Qaddah, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both)
Imam Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who bowed (in prayer) but did not recite the glorifications (subhana Rabbi al-Azim) out of forgetfulness; he said, 'His prayer is valid.'
ai.seo_question: Does forgetting to say the glorifications in ruku' invalidate the prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, transmitted via the chain of Abdullah al-Qaddah, the Imam clarifies that the omission of recommended glorifications (tasbihat) in ruku' due to forgetfulness does not invalidate the prayer. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential distinction between obligatory pillars (arkan) and recommended acts (masnunat), affirming that minor omissions of the latter do not nullify the prayer's validity.
